newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF plans to allow firms to offer US-type funds.
newsitem.headline: MOF plans to allow firms to offer US-type funds.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) plans to draft a special law that will allow financial institutions to offer U.S. style mutual funds and set up special-purpose companies with the aim of helping them dispose of bad loans.
A senior MOF official said on Friday the law will allow Japanese investment trust fund companies to offer U.S. style mutual funds.

He also said that the new law would help make it easier for financial institutions to set up special-purpose companies. Special-purpose companies are normally set up to help firms dispose of bad loans by securitising collateralised property.

He said that further details of the new law will be discussed at a meeting of an advisory panel to the Finance Minister. He said that the government aims to submit bills on the new law and on revisions to the Securities and Exchange Law at the next regular session of parliament which is expected to start next January.
The advisory panel, the Securities and Exchange Council, is expected to make final proposals by June to promote the nation's "Big Bang" reforms to liberalise Japan's financial markets.

Earlier on Friday, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told reporters that the government aims to submit bills on various securities-related laws at the next regular session of parliament to help realise the Big Bang reforms.
